claims.text: The starting material is a homogeneous, conventional CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy.
Controlled composition modulation can create a nanohierarchical architecture combining nanograins and nanoprecipitates in CoCrFeNi.
A compositionally modulated nanohierarchical heterostructure can provide adaptive surface protection from room temperature to 800 °C.
At room or lower temperatures, coupled nanograins and nanoprecipitates provide multiple deformation pathways that release frictional stress in stages.
Staged frictional-stress release reduces the coefficient of friction at lower temperatures.
At high temperatures, the nanohierarchical structure accelerates tribo-oxidation kinetics.
High-temperature sliding can generate a dense nanocrystalline oxide glaze layer.
The nanocrystalline glaze layer minimizes adhesive and oxidative wear and can provide solid lubrication.
The modified CoCrFeNi alloy will have a lower coefficient of friction than homogeneous CoCrFeNi throughout approximately 25–800 °C.
The modified CoCrFeNi alloy will have a lower wear rate than homogeneous CoCrFeNi throughout approximately 25–800 °C.
Homogeneous CoCrFeNi exhibits increased friction and wear challenges at elevated temperatures.
Environmental oxygen can contribute to tribo-oxidation and glaze formation during high-temperature sliding.
The proposed comparison should cover approximately 25–800 °C under a constant load of about 5 N.
The proposed comparison should include both inert and oxygen-containing environments.

contradictions.description: The high-temperature protection mechanism depends on tribo-oxidation and an oxide glaze, yet the hypothesis predicts consistent protection under inert as well as oxygen-containing conditions without identifying an oxygen-independent high-temperature mechanism for the inert tests.
